title: Direct observation of a spin-polarized surface Dirac gap in the antiferromagnetic topological insulator NdBi
authors: Yuto Fukushima, Hiroyuki S. Suzuki, Masayuki Ochi, Takuma Nishida, Toshiya Ikenobe, Hiraku Saito, Yuto Kinoshita, Kaishu Kawaguchi, Hiroaki Tanaka, Ayumi Harasawa, Takushi Iimori, Koichiro Yaji, Masashi Tokunaga, Taro Nakajima, Kiyohisa Tanaka, Takahiro Morimoto, Ryo Mori, Takeshi Kondo
abstract: A gapped Dirac cone in antiferromagnetic topological insulators (AFM-TIs) is essential for realizing the quantized anomalous Hall effect, yet its intrinsic magnitude remains controversial. In the prototypical AFM-TI MnBi2Te4, however, the observed Dirac gap is significantly smaller than theoretical predictions or nearly absent, highlighting a long-standing discrepancy. Here we demonstrate that NdBi hosts a spin-polarized topological surface Dirac cone with a sizable gap of 17 meV at the Dirac point, in excellent agreement with density functional theory predictions (12 meV). This direct observation is enabled by high-resolution 7 eV laser-based spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, which unambiguously disentangles the spin-polarized surface Dirac cone from bulk-derived states. Furthermore, through temperature dependence and controlled surface contamination, we establish a direct linkage between surface magnetism and the Dirac gap, demonstrating that the gap opens only in the presence of surface magnetic order. These results provide definitive spectroscopic evidence for an intrinsic Dirac gap in AFM-TIs and establish NdBi as a model platform to resolve the long-standing discrepancy between experiment and theory in AFM-TIs.
summary: This work provides definitive spectroscopic evidence for an intrinsic, spin-polarized Dirac gap in the AFM-TI $	ext{NdBi}$. By using high-resolution ARPES, the authors successfully distinguish the surface state gap from bulk features, confirming that the gap opens only when surface magnetism is established. This resolves a major theoretical discrepancy in the field and establishes $	ext{NdBi}$ as a model system for studying topological magnetism.
main_problem: The paper addresses the long-standing discrepancy regarding the magnitude and origin of the Dirac gap in Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulators (AFM-TIs). It aims to definitively observe the intrinsic surface Dirac gap.
main_result: The authors directly observed a sizable, spin-polarized surface Dirac gap ($\sim 17 	ext{ meV}$) in $	ext{NdBi}$ that opens only when surface magnetic order is present, confirming its intrinsic nature.
method: The study combines high-resolution spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) with Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, supplemented by temperature and contamination studies.
model_or_system: The physical system is the antiferromagnetic topological insulator $	ext{NdBi}$, which is studied in both paramagnetic (PM) and antiferromagnetic (AFM) phases. The analysis focuses on the topological surface Dirac cone (TSSC) and its coupling to the bulk electronic structure.
key_observables: Dirac gap magnitude ($\Delta_{	ext{gap}}$), spin polarization of the surface cone, temperature dependence of the gap, and magnetic order parameter ($\sqrt{I_{110}}$).
important_parameters: Observed gap ($\sim 17 	ext{ meV}$), DFT prediction ($\sim 12 	ext{ meV}$), Néel temperature ($T_N \approx 24 	ext{ K}$), and critical exponent $ eta$ matching the 3D Ising model.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that high-resolution ARPES can successfully disentangle the intrinsic topological surface state from bulk contributions, and that the gap opening is directly driven by surface magnetic order.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate electronic structures in different magnetic domains (PM vs. AFM), show the temperature evolution of the hybridization gap ($\Delta_{Hyb}$), and map the spin polarization of the surface states across the magnetic transition.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence by first establishing the necessity of high-resolution ARPES to separate surface/bulk states. It then maps the electronic structure across magnetic domains, quantifies the gap opening, and finally correlates the gap's temperature dependence and critical scaling with the bulk magnetic order parameter.
why_interesting: The rigorous experimental and theoretical confirmation of a gap opening linked directly to magnetic order in a topological material provides a robust platform for studying magnetoelectric coupling and topological quantum phenomena, which are key areas in condensed matter theory.
